blocks.text:
Rio offers city panoramas, the ocean and Brazil’s best-known landmarks. Iguazu changes the scale of the journey: streets and beaches give way to rainforest, a canyon and hundreds of streams of water. After the sightseeing, five nights in Búzios give you time to relax by the sea, try different beaches and enjoy water activities.

The first four nights in Rio give you time to see several sides of the city. Sugar Loaf reveals the coastline, the bay and the mountains around the centre, while Corcovado offers a wider view of the city. There is also a free day for nature, history or another view: the Botanical Garden, Petrópolis, the tropical islands, an evening show or a short helicopter flight.

At Iguazu, the programme lets you compare both sides. The Brazilian side makes it easier to see the full line of cascades and appreciate the scale of the falls. On the Argentine side, the walkways bring you closer to the water and are divided into the Lower Circuit, the Upper Circuit and the route to the Devil’s Throat. The two sightseeing days therefore complement each other.

The pace then deliberately slows down. Búzios takes up almost half of the remaining time, with no fixed sightseeing schedule. Choose a beach, water activities, walks and restaurants, or simply spend a day by the sea. After the city tours and waterfalls, this sequence lets you finish the journey with a proper seaside break.
